title: Corporate Tax Avoidance and Sales: Microevidence and Aggregate Implications
eligible_reason: The only DiD (Table 3, 'Alternative identification strategies') is a two-period, single-adoption-date design: MNE x Post1998 compares US multinationals with domestic firms before (1993-1996) and after (1999-2004) the 1997 check-the-box regulations and SFAS 131. All firms are treated at the same date, so there is no staggered adoption. The specification also includes time-varying controls (share of intangibles, labor productivity, acquisition dummy) and sector x period FE, and the paper's main strategy is OLS/2SLS with an IV for tax avoidance.
design_notes: Compustat firm-level data, 1994-2017, six 4-year windows; dependent variable log sales at end of window. Table 3: Diff-in-Diff cols (1) sector x period FE, (4) + firm FE; 2SLS cols use MNE x Post1998 as instrument for HS tax gap. Robust SEs, not clustered (Abadie et al. 2023 argument), firm-clustered version in Online Appendix OA.1. Online Appendix Table OA.13 repeats with Post1996. Text screened is the HAL working paper (halshs-04103835).
estimators_reported: OLS with sector x period FE / firm FE

specs.outcome: log sales at end of 6-year window
specs.treatment_definition: MNE status x indicator for 1999-2004 window (single policy date: CTB 1997 / SFAS 131 Dec 1998)
specs.fe: sector x period FE (no firm FE)
specs.controls: share of intangibles, labor productivity, acquisition dummy, MNE status (time-varying firm controls)
specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date, two periods; time-varying controls; no firm FE

specs.outcome: log sales at end of window
specs.fe: firm FE + sector x period FE
specs.controls: share of intangibles, labor productivity, acquisition dummy
specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date, two periods; time-varying controls

screener_notes: ft_staggered / ft_difference_in_differences flags are incidental. Compustat is licensed data. No staggered variation anywhere in the paper.
